messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired — P1 — region: az2 — symptom: NIC errors & elevated 5xx for serving nodes. page_id=PD-az2-4929999999. auto-repeat=3

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-az2-4929999999. On-call: @Maya Chen. Escalation policy: az-network.

Maya Chen: acked. I'm on it. pulling logs now.

Arjun Patel: seeing a spike in shard-level connection resets from the fabric logs — likely NIC/driver flapping after the 03:12 kernel roll.

Eva Morales: confirm: Hosted API latencies up ~2.3x for a subset of AZ2 pools, Dedicated customers hitting token generation timeouts ~10% increase, some 502s. Customers with cross-region routing are OK.

James Li: tagging runbook: az-network-failover (runbook link: https://redwood/runbooks/az-network-failover). follow step 1 -> verify spine health.

oncall-sre: running quick health probes against the az2 serving pool. output: 
```
for node in $(cat az2-nodes.txt); do curl -sS http://$node:9090/health || echo "DOWN $node"; done
# sample failures: node-az2-17 DOWN, node-az2-22 DOWN, node-az2-09 DOWN
```

Maya Chen: good catch. I'm starting controlled divert for model-serving traffic routed to az3 for non-low-latency customers. will keep latency-sensitive routes on AZ3 only.

Arjun Patel: can we activate fallback policy in routing layer? prefer automated fallback to az3 for host=*.redwood-inference.com except customers with pinned AZ2 (dedicated).

Maya Chen: yes applying routing rule now. patch:
```
POST /routing/policies/activate
{ "policy": "az2-evac-divert-2026-03-15", "match": "region:az2 AND customer_type!=dedicated", "action": "route:az3", "ttl": 1800 }
```

Maya Chen: rule applied. traffic diverted ~40% in last 60s. monitoring logs.

Eva Morales: adding customer impact note for ops -> statuspage: high error rate for a subset of az2-backed endpoints, partial mitigations in place via cross-AZ routing. ETA for full restoration unknown.

James Li: opening network infra PD ticket and pinging @Arjun Patel (network lead) for kernel rollback consideration.

Arjun Patel: we should avoid full kernel rollback unless infra approves. quick mitigation: disable hardware offload on affected NICs on nodes 17/22/09. rolling those nodes out of pool now.

oncall-sre: rolling replacement started. draining node-az2-17 -> cordon -> reboot -> re-enable. steps logged in ops-runbook.

incident-bot: update: PD-az2-4929999999 status=acknowledged; responders=Maya Chen, Arjun Patel, James Li.

Maya Chen: status update for the channel: 03:25 — automated page for az2 NIC errors; immediate mitigation: routing divert to az3 for non-dedicated traffic implemented; several bad nodes drained; replacement in progress. Visible customer impact: elevated latencies and 502s for az2-leading requests; majority of traffic now served from az3 after divert.

Eva Morales: preparing a short statuspage draft: 
"We are investigating increased errors and latency for services backed by AZ2. Traffic for many customers has been routed to AZ3 to reduce impact. Dedicated customers pinned to AZ2 may see degraded performance. Engineering is working on node remediation. Updates every 15 minutes."

Maya Chen: good. please post once we have confirmation of stable health probes for >10m.

Arjun Patel: replacement nodes are coming up healthy. NIC offload disable applied via ansible on the remaining at-risk nodes. kernel rollback avoided.

oncall-sre: health probe summary: 10/12 nodes healthy; 2 nodes still flapping but drained. error rate back to ~8% above baseline (was 40%).

Maya Chen: moving to monitoring mode. if error rate <10% and stable for 10m we can start gradual reweighting from az3 -> az2 for non-pinned traffic. scheduling that now — reweight step 1/4.

incident-bot: PD-az2-4929999999 note: next automated reminder in 15m.

James Li: after-action: create action items — (1) follow up with infra to validate firmware on affected NIC batch, (2) add automated healthcheck to trigger pre-divert when node-level 5xx > 15% for 30s, (3) add clearer label on Dedicated customers that prevents auto-divert without explicit approval.

Maya Chen: agree. documenting timeline for postmortem. will handoff to SRE rotations in 30m.

Arjun Patel: ping me when postmortem draft is ready; I have metrics to add (fabric counters, driver logs).

incident-bot: PD-az2-4929999999 status=monitoring.

Maya Chen: handing off to oncall-sre for continued monitoring. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: acknowledged handoff — monitoring + 15m check-ins. will escalate to infra if any new node flaps.

incident-bot: thread closed by Maya Chen (manual close) — final note: partial divert to az3 mitigated customer impact; remediation in progress; postmortem to follow.
